title: “Because of You” by Tony Bennett with Percy Faith
text: "Because of You" is a popular song written by Arthur Hammerstein and Dudley Wilkinson in 1940. It was first recorded by Larry Clinton and His Orchestra on December 12, 1940, and was released March 28, 1941 on Bluebird 11094.
listen: Because of You Tony Bennett with Percy Faith

title: “How High the Moon” by Les Paul and Mary Ford
text: "How High the Moon" is a jazz standard with lyrics by Nancy Hamilton and music by Morgan Lewis. It was first featured in the 1940 Broadway revue Two for the Show, where it was sung by Alfred Drake and Frances Comstock.
listen: How High the Moon Les Paul and Mary Ford

title: “Come On-a My House” by Rosemary Clooney
text: "Come On-a My House" is a song written by Ross Bagdasarian and William Saroyan and originally released by Rosemary Clooney in 1951. Bagdasarian and Saroyan were cousins who wrote the song while driving across New Mexico in the summer of 1939.
listen: Come On-a My House Rosemary Clooney

title: “Be My Love” by Mario Lanza with Ray Sinatra and Jeff Alexander
text: "Be My Love" is a song with lyrics by Sammy Cahn and music by Nicholas Brodszky. Published in 1950, it was written for Mario Lanza, who sang it with Kathryn Grayson in the 1950 movie The Toast of New Orleans.
listen: Be My Love Mario Lanza with Ray Sinatra and Jeff Alexander

title: “On Top of Old Smoky” by The Weavers and Terry Gilkyson with Vic Schoen
text: "On Top of Old Smoky" is a traditional folk song and nursery rhyme of the United States. It is catalogued as Roud Folk Song Index No.
listen: On Top of Old Smoky The Weavers and Terry Gilkyson with Vic Schoen

title: “Cold, Cold Heart” by Tony Bennett with Percy Faith
text: "Cold, Cold Heart" is a country music and pop song written and first recorded by Hank Williams. This blues ballad is both a classic of honky-tonk and an entry in the Great American Songbook.
listen: Cold, Cold Heart Tony Bennett with Percy Faith

title: “If” by Perry Como with Mitchell Ayres
text: "If" is a popular song with music written by Tolchard Evans and the lyrics written by Robert Hargreaves and Stanley J. Damerell. The song was written in 1934, but the most popular versions were recorded in 1950–1951.
listen: If Perry Como with Mitchell Ayres

title: “The Loveliest Night of the Year” by Mario Lanza
text: "The Loveliest Night of the Year" is a popular song. The music was first published as a waltz called "Sobre las olas" in 1888, written by Juventino P. Rosas.
wiki: The Loveliest Night of the Year
listen: The Loveliest Night of the Year Mario Lanza

title: “Tennessee Waltz” by Patti Page
text: "Tennessee Waltz" is an American popular country music song with lyrics by Redd Stewart and music by Pee Wee King written in 1946 and first released in January 1948. The song became a multimillion seller via a 1950 recording – as "The Tennessee Waltz" – by Patti Page.
listen: Tennessee Waltz Patti Page

title: “Jezebel” by Frankie Laine with The Norman Luboff Choir and Mitch Miller
text: "Jezebel" is a 1951 popular song written by American songwriter Wayne Shanklin. It was recorded by Frankie Laine with the Norman Luboff Choir and Mitch Miller and his orchestra on April 4, 1951 and released by Columbia Records as catalog number 39367.
listen: Jezebel Frankie Laine with The Norman Luboff Choir and Mitch Miller

title: “I Get Ideas” by Tony Martin with Henri René
text: "I Get Ideas" is a popular song which has been recorded by various musicians and used in a number of films and television episodes.
listen: I Get Ideas Tony Martin with Henri René

title: “Mockin' Bird Hill” by Les Paul and Mary Ford
text: "Mockin' Bird Hill" is a song written in 3⁄4 time by Calle Jularbo, with lyrics by George Vaughn Horton. It is perhaps best known through recordings by Patti Page, Horton's own Pinetoppers, and the duo of Les Paul and Mary Ford in 1951, or by Donna Fargo's 1977 version, but many other artists have also recorded the song.
listen: Mockin' Bird Hill Les Paul and Mary Ford

title: “My Heart Cries for You” by Guy Mitchell & Mitch Miller
text: "My Heart Cries for You" is a popular song, adapted by Carl Sigman and Percy Faith from an 18th-century French melody. The song has been recorded by many singers, the most successful of which was recorded by Guy Mitchell.
listen: My Heart Cries for You Guy Mitchell & Mitch Miller

title: “Sound Off” by Vaughn Monroe
text: Vaughn Wilton Monroe was an American baritone singer, trumpeter and big band leader who was most popular in the 1940s and 1950s. He has two stars on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, one for recording and another for radio performance.
listen: Sound Off Vaughn Monroe

title: “Sweet Violets” by Dinah Shore with Henri René
text: "Sweet Violets" is an American song that contains classic example of a "censored rhyme", where the expected rhyme of each couplet or verse is replaced with a surprising word which segues into the next couplet or chorus. For example, the first couplets of the version recorded by Dinah Shore are: There once was a farmer who took a young miss In back of the barn where he gave her a...

title: “The World Is Waiting for the Sunrise” by Les Paul and Mary Ford
text: "The World Is Waiting for the Sunrise" is a post-World War I popular song with lyrics by Canadian-born American actor Eugene Lockhart, and music composed by Canadian-born concert pianist Ernest Seitz in 1918. He later claimed he conceived the refrain when he was 12 years old.
wiki: The World Is Waiting for the Sunrise
listen: The World Is Waiting for the Sunrise Les Paul and Mary Ford

title: “My Truly, Truly Fair” by Guy Mitchell & Mitch Miller
text: "My Truly, Truly Fair" is a popular song written by Bob Merrill. It was published in 1951.
listen: My Truly, Truly Fair Guy Mitchell & Mitch Miller

title: “Aba Daba Honeymoon” by Debbie Reynolds & Carleton Carpenter with Georgie Stoll
text: "Aba Daba Honeymoon" is a show tune with lyrics by Arthur Fields and music by Walter Donovan. It was published in 1914 by Leo Feist.

title: “Rose, Rose, I Love You” by Frankie Laine and The Norman Luboff Choir with Paul Weston
text: "Rose, Rose, I Love You" is a 1940 Mandarin popular song composed by Chen Gexin and first recorded by Yao Lee. An English-language version whose lyrics have little in common with the original Mandarin was first recorded by Frankie Laine in 1951.

text: "I Apologize" is a popular song written by Al Hoffman, Al Goodhart, and Ed Nelson.

title: “You're Just in Love” by Perry Como & The Fontane Sisters with Mitchell Ayres
text: "You're Just in Love" is a popular song by Irving Berlin. It was published in 1950 and was first performed by Ethel Merman and Russell Nype in Call Me Madam, a musical comedy that made its debut at the Imperial Theatre in New York City on October 12 that year.

text: "Undecided" is a popular song written by Sid Robin with music by Charlie Shavers and published in 1938.

title: “The Thing” by Phil Harris with Walter Scharf
text: "The Thing" is a novelty song by Charles Randolph Grean released in 1950. The song received heavy airplay, spending 14 weeks on the Billboard charts.
listen: The Thing Phil Harris with Walter Scharf

title: Say It with Acting
text: Say It With Acting is an American television game show that was broadcast on NBC from January 8, 1951, until May 1951, and on ABC from August 1951 until February 22, 1952.

title: With This Ring
text: With This Ring is a prime time panel show aired by the DuMont Television Network on Sundays from January 21, 1951, to March 11, 1951. The show featured engaged couples who had recently applied for a marriage license.

title: Public Prosecutor
text: Public Prosecutor is an American television series produced in 1947–1948, which first aired in 1951. It was the first dramatic series to be shot on film instead of being performed and broadcast live.

title: The Victor Borge Show
text: The Victor Borge Show is a 30-minute American variety television program that was broadcast live on NBC from February 3, 1951, to June 30, 1951. It was sponsored by Kellogg.

title: Ladies Before Gentlemen
text: Ladies Before Gentlemen is an American television series that aired on the DuMont Television Network from February 28 to May 2, 1951. It was a panel show which featured discussions of male and female perspectives on a variety of topics.

title: Watch Mr. Wizard
text: Watch Mr. Wizard is an American children's television series that demonstrates the science behind ordinary things.

title: Once Upon a Tune
text: Once Upon a Tune is a weekly half-hour American musical anthology television series that aired on the DuMont Television Network, premiering on March 6, 1951, and running to May 15, 1951.

title: Miss Susan
text: Miss Susan is a daytime drama that aired on NBC from March 12 to December 28, 1951. The main writer was William Kendall Clarke.

title: Beat the Clock
text: Beat the Clock is an American television game show. Contestants attempt to complete challenges such as physical stunts within a time limit in order to win prizes.

title: The Range Rider
text: The Range Rider is an American Western television series that was first broadcast in syndication from 1951 to 1952. A single lost episode surfaced and was broadcast in 1959.

title: Major Dell Conway of the Flying Tigers
text: Major Dell Conway of the Flying Tigers is an early American television program broadcast on the now defunct DuMont Television Network. The series ran from April 7, 1951, to March 2, 1952.
wiki: Major Dell Conway of the Flying Tigers

title: DuMont Royal Theater
text: DuMont Royal Theater is an American dramatic anthology television series which ran on the now-defunct DuMont Television Network from April 12, 1951, to June 26, 1952. The half-hour series ran during the summers, and in 1952 it ran on alternate weeks with Gruen Playhouse.

title: The Adventures of Wild Bill Hickok
text: The Adventures of Wild Bill Hickok is an American Western television series that ran for eight seasons from April 15, 1951, through September 24, 1958. The Screen Gems series began in syndication, but ran on CBS from June 5, 1955, through 1958, and, at the same time, on ABC from 1957 through 1958.
wiki: The Adventures of Wild Bill Hickok

title: Music From Chicago
text: Music from Chicago was a music and variety program broadcast on the DuMont Television Network from April 15, 1951 to June 17, 1951. It was broadcast on Sundays from 9:30 to 10 p.m.

title: Casey, Crime Photographer
text: Casey, Crime Photographer is an American crime drama television series that aired from April 19, 1951, to June 5, 1952, on the CBS Television Network. The series ran for 57 episodes over two seasons.

title: Not for Publication
text: Not for Publication is an American crime drama TV series which aired on the now-defunct DuMont Television Network from April 1951 to May 1952. The series was also known as Reporter Collins.

title: Stage Entrance
text: Stage Entrance is an American variety and interview television show broadcast on the DuMont Television Network.

title: Pentagon
text: Pentagon, a.k.a. Pentagon Washington, is a public affairs TV series broadcast by the DuMont Television Network from May 6, 1951, to November 24, 1952.

title: Jacqueline Susann's Open Door
text: Jacqueline Susann's Open Door is an American discussion show hosted by Jacqueline Susann, later to become famous as the author of Valley of the Dolls. It aired nationally on the DuMont Television Network between May 7 and June 18, 1951.

title: Strike It Rich
text: Strike It Rich was a game show that was broadcast on American radio from June 29, 1947, to December 27, 1957, on CBS and NBC. It was broadcast on television as well, starting in 1951. Billed as “The quiz show with a heart”, people in need of money appeared and told their tale of woe, then tried to win money by answering four questions.

title: Quo Vadis
text: Quo Vadis is a 1951 American religious epic historical film set in ancient Rome during the final years of Emperor Nero's reign, based on the 1896 novel of the same title by Polish Nobel Laureate author Henryk Sienkiewicz. Produced by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer and filmed in Technicolor, it was directed by Mervyn LeRoy from a screenplay by S. N. Behrman, Sonya Levien, and John Lee Mahin.

title: Show Boat
text: Show Boat is a 1951 American musical romantic drama film, based on the 1927 stage musical of the same name by Jerome Kern and Oscar Hammerstein II (script and lyrics), and the 1926 novel by Edna Ferber. It was made by MGM, adapted for the screen by John Lee Mahin, produced by Arthur Freed and directed by George Sidney.

title: David and Bathsheba
text: David and Bathsheba is a 1951 American epic film produced by 20th Century-Fox and starring Gregory Peck as King David. It was directed by Henry King and produced by Darryl F. Zanuck, with a screenplay by Philip Dunne and cinematography by Leon Shamroy.

title: The Great Caruso
text: The Great Caruso is a 1951 biographical film directed by Richard Thorpe, produced by Joe Pasternak, distributed by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer and starring Mario Lanza as operatic tenor Enrico Caruso. The highly fictionalized screenplay, written by Sonya Levien and William Ludwig, is based on the biography Enrico Caruso His Life and Death by Dorothy Caruso, Caruso's widow.

title: A Streetcar Named Desire
text: A Streetcar Named Desire is a 1951 American Southern Gothic drama film adapted from Tennessee Williams' Pulitzer Prize-winning play of the same name. Directed by Elia Kazan, it stars Vivien Leigh, Marlon Brando, Kim Hunter, and Karl Malden.

title: The African Queen
text: The African Queen is a 1951 adventure film adapted from the 1935 novel of the same name by C. S. Forester. It was directed by John Huston and produced by Sam Spiegel, and John Woolf.

title: That's My Boy
text: That's My Boy is a 1951 American musical comedy film directed by Hal Walker and starring the comedy team of Martin and Lewis.

title: An American in Paris
text: An American in Paris is a 1951 American musical romantic comedy film inspired by the 1928 jazz-influenced symphonic poem An American in Paris by George Gershwin. Starring Gene Kelly, Leslie Caron (her film debut), Oscar Levant, Georges Guétary, and Nina Foch, the film is set in Paris and was directed by Vincente Minnelli from a script by Alan Jay Lerner.

title: A Place in the Sun
text: A Place in the Sun is a 1951 American tragedy film directed and produced by George Stevens from a screenplay by Harry Brown and Michael Wilson, based on the 1925 novel An American Tragedy by Theodore Dreiser and its 1926 stage adaptation by Patrick Kearney. It stars Montgomery Clift, Elizabeth Taylor, Shelley Winters and Keefe Brasselle.
wiki: A Place in the Sun (1951 film)

title: At War with the Army
text: At War with the Army is a 1950 American musical comedy film directed by Hal Walker and released by Paramount Pictures. It stars the comedy team of Martin and Lewis and introduces Polly Bergen.

title: List of highest-grossing films in India
text: This ranking lists the highest-grossing films in India, based on domestic box office estimates as reported by organizations classified as green by Wikipedia. The figures are not adjusted for inflation.
wiki: List of highest-grossing films in India

title: Cinema of Italy
text: The cinema of Italy comprises the films made within Italy or by Italian directors. Since its beginning, Italian cinema has influenced film movements worldwide.

title: Cinema of Japan
text: The cinema of Japan, also known domestically as hōga (邦画; "domestic cinema"), began in the late 1890s. Japan has one of the oldest and largest film industries in the world; as of 2022, it was the fourth largest by number of feature films produced (634) and the third largest in terms of box office revenue ($1.5 billion).

title: List of Soviet films of the year by ticket sales
text: This is the list of highest-grossing films in the Soviet Union, in terms of box office admissions. It includes the highest-grossing films in the Soviet Union (USSR), the highest-grossing domestic Soviet films, the domestic films with the greatest number of ticket sales by year, and the highest-grossing foreign films in the Soviet Union.
wiki: List of highest-grossing films in the Soviet Union

title: Soviet space dogs Dezik and Tsygan become the first to enter space, in a 15-minute sub-orbital spaceflight from Kapustin Yar in an R-1 rocket, being safely parachuted back to earth.
text: In the 1950s and 1960s, the Soviet space program used dogs for suborbital and orbital space flights as proof-of-concept to determine whether human spaceflight was feasible. The Soviet space program typically used female dogs due to their anatomical compatibility with the spacesuit.

title: Janie Moore, C. S. Lewis' so-called adoptive mother, dies.
text: Clive Staples Lewis was a British author, literary scholar and Anglican lay theologian. He held academic positions in English literature at both Magdalen College, Oxford (1925–1954), and Magdalene College, Cambridge (1954–1963).

title: The American writer Flannery O'Connor leaves hospital after being diagnosed with lupus at the age of 25.
text: Mary Flannery O'Connor was an American novelist, short story writer, and essayist. She wrote two novels and 31 short stories, as well as a number of reviews and commentaries.

title: Hank Ketcham's American comic strip Dennis the Menace first appears in 16 American newspapers. The strip is originally distributed by the Post-Hall Syndicate.
text: Henry King Ketcham was an American cartoonist who created the Dennis the Menace comic strip, writing and drawing it from 1951 to 1994, when he retired from drawing the daily cartoon and took up painting full-time in his home studio. In 1953, he received the Reuben Award for the strip, which continues today in the hands of other cartoonists.

title: The homonymous British comic strip Dennis the Menace first appears in the Scottish anthology comic magazine The Beano, in issue 452 (dated March 17, 1951), on sale from March 12. It is the longest-running strip in the comic. The idea and…
text: Music hall is a type of British theatrical entertainment that was most popular from the early Victorian era until around World War I. It faded away after 1918 as the halls rebranded their entertainment as variety. Perceptions of a distinction in Britain between bold and scandalous music hall entertainment and subsequent, more respectable variety entertainment differ.

title: Spring – Arthur C. Clarke's short story "The Sentinel", which will form a basis for the film 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) and a subsequent novel, is published as "Sentinel of Eternity" in the only issue ever produced of the American…
text: Sir Arthur Charles Clarke was an English science fiction writer, inventor, undersea explorer and TV series host. He popularised space travel and wrote many books and many essays for popular magazines.

title: Joe Orton enters the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London, where he meets his lover and ultimate murderer Kenneth Halliwell.
text: The Royal Academy of Dramatic Art is a drama school in London, England, which provides vocational conservatoire training for theatre, film, television, and radio. It is based in Bloomsbury, Central London, close to the Senate House complex of the University of London, and is a founding member of the Federation of Drama Schools.

title: Frank Hardy is acquitted of criminal libel in the Australian state of Victoria over his self-published 1950 roman à clef on corruption in Melbourne political life, Power Without Glory.
text: Francis Joseph Hardy, published as Frank J. Hardy and also under the pseudonym Ross Franklyn, was an Australian novelist and writer. He is best known for his 1950 novel Power Without Glory, and for his later political activism.

title: J. D. Salinger's coming-of-age story The Catcher in the Rye is published by Little, Brown and Company in New York City.
text: Jerome David Salinger was an American writer best known for his 1951 novel The Catcher in the Rye. Salinger published several short stories in Story magazine in 1940, before serving in World War II. In 1948, his critically acclaimed story "A Perfect Day for Bananafish" appeared in The New Yorker, which published much of his later work.

title: The Peggy Guggenheim Collection at the Palazzo Venier dei Leoni in Venice is first opened to the public.
text: The Peggy Guggenheim Collection is an art museum on the Grand Canal in the Dorsoduro sestiere of Venice, Italy. It is one of the most visited attractions in Venice.

title: Festival Star emblem by Abram Games.
text: The Festival Star was the graphic symbol designed by Abram Games for the 1951 Festival of Britain. Games was one of 12 artists invited to submit designs to the Arts Council and the Council of Industrial Design in 1948, and won the limited competition.

title: Royal Festival Hall by Leslie Martin, Peter Moro and Robert Matthew.
text: Sir John Leslie Martin was an English architect, and a leading advocate of the International Style. Martin's most famous building is the Royal Festival Hall.

title: Dome of Discovery by Ralph Tubbs.
text: The Dome of Discovery was a temporary exhibition building designed by architect Ralph Tubbs for the Festival of Britain celebrations which took place on London's South Bank in 1951, alongside the River Thames. The consulting engineers were Freeman Fox & Partners, in particular Oleg Kerensky and Gilbert Roberts.

title: Skylon by Philip Powell, Hidalgo Moya and Felix Samuely.
text: The Skylon was a futuristic-looking, slender, vertical, cigar-shaped steel tensegrity structure located by the Thames in London, that gave the illusion of floating above the ground, built in 1951 for the Festival of Britain. A popular joke of the period was that, like the British economy of 1951, "It had no visible means of support".
